evidence_limitations: No authenticated full-workflow completion, hardware gesture, VoiceOver journey or haptic certification. Native supplemental images establish software-keyboard geometry only, not completion or hardware behavior.
Native Morning receipt means seeded core receipt plus comments-error only.
Native morning-score images show live scene and cannot prove a completed score interaction.
Native 17pro morning-kept dark-large image shows live Hole 15 and is excluded as kept/resume evidence.
Stale SE3 light-large Door contact-sheet blank was superseded by valid direct PNG; blank itself was not scored.
Book receipt-named screenshot remains overview, so receipt-selection behavior is unscored.
Home fixture provides lead/deck only, not a full server read model.

overall_specificity: Cup Season has a coherent, golf-specific language in the native live round, receipt and public round. The web is less coherent where older generic card/stat sections remain. Preserve the authored system; priority is legibility and task order, not a new aesthetic.

priority_findings.title: Email entry has no persistent or programmatic label
evidence: Fresh isolated IAB tab: email text field was unnamed in AX tree; read-only DOM inspection found no label and no aria-label.
priority_findings.why: A screen-reader user reaches an unnamed field; the placeholder is also the only visible email cue and disappears during entry.
priority_findings.remedy: Give the field a persistent Email label associated through for/id; preserve the existing code-only auth behavior.

priority_findings.title: Home occasion panel uses page ink on an inverted panel
priority_findings.why: The dark capture has nearly white heading on pale panel; the light capture reverses into dark text on dark panel. The opportunity cannot be read reliably.
priority_findings.remedy: Render this prose on its page ground, or use the existing paired panel ink for every text role. Keep the ordinary action on act under D359.

priority_findings.title: AX3 live-round context displaces the scoring controls
priority_findings.why: On SE3 AX3, course/tee/rating, setup, sync status, hole header and the stacked score legend fill almost the entire screen before the first golfer; the first plus/minus controls require a scroll.
priority_findings.remedy: At accessibility sizes place the current hole and current golfer controls before secondary course/tee metadata and strip legend, or disclose those secondary details. Preserve full text scaling and truthful sync status.

priority_findings.title: Filled tee details lose their visible individual labels
priority_findings.why: The setup displays a tee word followed by two bare numbers. AX3 stacks them into separate rows, but the collective Tee & rating heading still does not identify the slope value. Accessibility labels exist in source; this finding is visual recognition.
priority_findings.remedy: Keep compact visible Tee, Rating and Slope labels associated with the filled fields, especially in the AX3 stacked form.

priority_findings.title: First-round composer spends most of its length explaining league math
priority_findings.why: A brand-new golfer has no league, yet the screen continues from an empty score into a league-points panel and all five point bands. The core course/score task competes with explanation that does not yet apply to their competition.
priority_findings.remedy: For the no-league first-round state, keep the course/score task and a short consequence sentence visible; disclose the existing point-band explanation from a named help control. Do not change scoring.

priority_findings.title: Empty profile repeats the absence of a record
priority_findings.why: The credential shows zero rounds, then an empty trophy case, four empty statistics, another no-rounds section and an empty courses section. The golfer must pass several statements of absence before the next useful action.
priority_findings.remedy: Keep the identity card and one first-round next step; reveal the record sections as data arrives, using the existing record grammar and without removing access to relevant actions.

priority_findings.title: Book status letters merge visually into point totals
priority_findings.why: Cells read as 33D, 22D or 16*D at the same typographic scale. The key explaining Dropped appears below the table, out of the narrow first viewport. A first-time reader must decode what is points and what is a status.
priority_findings.remedy: Give the existing status marker visual separation and a smaller record role; place a compact legend next to the display selector or provide the status in the cell accessible name. Preserve the exact Book semantics and receipt path.

priority_findings.title: Compete empty state repeats its primary invitation
priority_findings.why: Start something appears beside the title and again beneath the empty story. Two equal invitations dilute the one useful decision on a screen with little content.
priority_findings.remedy: Keep the primary Start something at the empty-state action group and let the farther title action go quiet for this state, following one fact, one place.

priority_findings.title: Legal leaves the shared paper and action palette
priority_findings.why: Legal switches to cool white/gray cards and gold or orange ordinary navigation while Get and Support retain the shared warm paper/green-black system. Reading remains clear, but the transition looks like a different product.
priority_findings.remedy: Use existing ground/ink/act tokens for the standalone document shell, retaining its prose layout and all legal text.

priority_findings.title: The web round-share artifact repeats its performance band
priority_findings.why: The central band label and immediately following sentence both say the golfer played to their handicap. The repetition takes space from the course/date facts and makes the share artifact more explanatory than memorable.
priority_findings.remedy: Use one existing named-band sentence for this branch of the share renderer, preserving all factual public fields and the approved pennant.

findings.title: Book status letters merge visually into point totals
findings.why: Cells read as 33D, 22D or 16*D at the same typographic scale. The key explaining Dropped appears below the table, out of the narrow first viewport. A first-time reader must decode what is points and what is a status.
findings.remedy: Give the existing status marker visual separation and a smaller record role; place a compact legend next to the display selector or provide the status in the cell accessible name. Preserve the exact Book semantics and receipt path.

findings.title: Compete empty state repeats its primary invitation
findings.why: Start something appears beside the title and again beneath the empty story. Two equal invitations dilute the one useful decision on a screen with little content.
findings.remedy: Keep the primary Start something at the empty-state action group and let the farther title action go quiet for this state, following one fact, one place.

persona_red_flags: First-time season member: D/* notation appears before its offscreen legend.
minor_observations: Book error keeps an instructional Behind the points panel even when there are no cells; minor dead instruction, not a blocker.
